outlook: Grains closed lower Tuesday. November soybeans fell 4 cents to $12.83¾ as traders waited for China to resume significant U.S. purchases after its national holiday and Brazil's soybean planting ran a record-fast 20% complete, while December corn was nearly unchanged at $4.82¾ as the market consolidated after last week's post-WASDE losses. Wheat was lower across all three exchanges, with Minneapolis December spring wheat down 2¼ cents to $6.94, after IKAR trimmed its Russian wheat crop estimate to 88.0 million tonnes; ICE November canola gave back C$3.40. USDA's holiday-delayed Crop Progress report showed corn harvest 33% done and soybeans 50% as of Oct 11, both ahead of the five-year average, with winter wheat 51% planted.
